memories.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.
Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.
The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.
A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.
HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.
Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.
Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.
Reviewers often inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns. The reference focuses on communicating branching procedures, prototype fidelity, reviewer attention, and diagram maintenance, while the compared frame specifies ethical and operational safeguards for field user studies. No shared, scoped, conflicting, or unclear claim is established.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one underlying presentation claim into a recommendation, drawing guidance, visual capability, and comprehension rationale; the compared frame provides no counterpart.
relations.summary: Flow diagrams are recommended for branching procedures because they show alternate paths and outcomes together and communicate the overall branching shape efficiently.

relations.reason: This independently useful reference-side distinction has no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A prototype’s visual fidelity and functional fidelity may differ.

relations.reason: The reference-side memories restate one reviewer-attention pattern at different levels of specificity, with no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: HCI reviewers often inspect a proposal’s primary visuals, including prototype screens and interaction-flow diagrams, before reading its full explanation.

relations.reason: This reference-side maintenance tradeoff is independently useful and is not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Updating a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than changing a single table row.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories express one requirement through authoring guidance and the ethics reviewer’s verification; the reference frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Anticipated participant burden and mitigation strategies should correspond for every field-study task and be reviewable on that basis.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories split one accessibility-planning claim into identifying accommodations and describing their delivery, without a reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Field-study plans should specify necessary accessibility accommodations and how they will be provided.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories combine an operational safeguard with its withdrawal-risk rationale; the reference frame does not address this policy.
relations.summary: Field participation requires a safe alternative work procedure so participants can withdraw and return to existing practices without undue risk.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers burden mitigation, accessibility, identifier separation, equipment loans, safe withdrawal, protection for nonparticipants, and the risk of underestimating workplace burden.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers flow diagrams for branching procedures, distinctions in prototype fidelity, reviewers’ tendency to inspect visuals first, and the maintenance cost of redrawing diagrams.
